definition: in a brief and clearly expressed manner
memoryTip: Succinct = cinched tight like a belt—short and clear.
correctPassage: The researcher summarized her findings succinctly, distilling months of data into a few precise claims.
wrongPassages: He described the proposal so succinctly that the presentation stretched well past the allotted hour.
The memo was written succinctly, wandering through several digressions before reaching its point.
She answered the question succinctly by repeating the same anecdote with ever more detail.

definition: showing great attention to correct detail or form
memoryTip: Punctual about points—picky about every detail of etiquette.
correctPassage: A punctilious archivist corrected every citation so that no source was incomplete or mislabeled.
wrongPassages: His punctilious review of the application skipped the required forms and ignored the dress code.
She was too punctilious to notice that the contract bore the wrong date and signature.
The punctilious clerk filed every document into a single unmarked drawer without sorting them.

correctPassage: An eldritch light over the marsh made the abandoned mill seem less abandoned than watching.
wrongPassages: The eldritch kitchen felt warm and ordinary after a long day of errands.
Neighbors described the eldritch block party as cheerful, familiar, and entirely predictable.
She preferred eldritch lighting that left every corner of the room bright and inviting.

memoryTip: Ob-fus-cate: cloud over—deliberately make it hard to understand.
correctPassage: Dense legal jargon can obfuscate responsibility rather than make it plain to the public.
wrongPassages: The diagram was redesigned to obfuscate the process so beginners could follow each step.
Teachers asked students to obfuscate their main claim in one clear, direct sentence.
The FAQ was rewritten to obfuscate common questions with plain-language answers.

memoryTip: Clear joints of speech—express ideas smoothly and clearly.
correctPassage: Few candidates could articulate a coherent plan for reforming the district's budget.
wrongPassages: He could only articulate in broken fragments that left the audience more confused than before.
She refused to articulate any position, remaining silent through the entire debate.
His attempt to articulate dissolved into mumbled half-sentences no one could parse.
